scope: LCS5 (End-of-Life) – Recyclability disruptors for Apparel & Footwear

resolution_policy.effect: If any matching rule evaluates to true, set R2 = 0 for the specified scope (product or pathway).
notes: Disruptors are evaluated per product. If a product-level disruptor is true, all recycling pathways (R2) for that product are set to 0.
If only pathway-level disruptors are true, only those pathways are set to R2=0; other pathways may remain available.
All shares (R2/R3) must be renormalized if pathways are disabled.

then.reason: EEE disruptor blocks textile recycling pathways for the whole product.

product_level.description: Non-textile materials (e.g., leather, coated fabrics, composites) dominate the product mass.

then.reason: Non-textile dominance disrupts textile recycling streams.

mechanical_wipers.description: Insufficient cotton content for wipers route.
Coatings, laminations or membrane layers present.

then.reason: Film layers disrupt rag cutting and absorption.
Metallic yarns contaminate wiping rags stream.

mechanical_wipers.description: Too many fibre types in blend.

then.reason: Elastane >5% degrades shredding density and bonding.

mechanical_insulation.description: Multi-layer composite (e.g., laminated membranes, PU coating).

then.reason: Composite layers disrupt uniform fibre feedstock.

mechanical_insulation.description: High share of trims/fasteners (metal/plastic) that cannot be removed.

then.reason: Non-fibre components disrupt shredding and contamination limits.

mechanical_textile_to_textile.description: Insufficient fibre purity for mechanical textile-to-textile.

then.reason: Pathway requires near-monopoly fibre type (single fibre).

mechanical_textile_to_textile.description: Short staple length or severe fabric damage (e.g., heavy brushing/raising).

then.reason: Insufficient fibre length for spinning recycled fibres.

chemical_textile_to_textile_synthetics.description: Insufficient PET/PA/PU purity for chemical recycling.

then.reason: Requires high polymer purity and limited contaminants.

chemical_textile_to_textile_cellulosics.description: Insufficient cellulose content or presence of non-cellulosic coatings.

then.reason: Requires very high cellulosic share and low contaminants.

product_level.description: Non-disassemblable multi-material construction (e.g., permanently bonded uppers/soles).

thermoplastic_material.description: Thermoplastic pathway requires high thermoplastic purity.
Use of thermoset/PU adhesives incompatible with re-melting.

reticulated_materials_PU_foam.description: Reticulated PU foams and cross-linked rubbers are not recyclable in default scenario.

then.reason: Cross-linked networks cannot be remelted or depolymerized per default.

notes: Thresholds reflect common defaults consistent with PEFCR logic. If you have verified industrial evidence of recyclability, you may override specific rules for a product with a documented R2 > 0.
If any pathway is disabled by disruptors, distribute the disabled R2 share to disposal (1 − R2 − R3) unless alternative evidence supports a different split.
For footwear, PEFCR default assumes negligible recycling (R2 ≈ 0). Pathways are provided here to support future evidence-based scenarios.
